subject: Proposal: rebalance of monthly service credit allocation & maintenance carve-out
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudbridge.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: Proposal: rebalance of monthly service credit allocation & maintenance carve-out

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudBridge is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Before we move to an MSA, we need to align on how monthly service credits are calculated for workloads that are heavily batch-oriented. A couple of specifics from our side:

- We operate a nightly batched inference window (00:00–06:00 CET) where jobs spike; occasional maintenance and scheduled model rollouts happen in that window.
- We can tolerate short interruptions during that window if scheduled in advance, but the standard SLA language (99.9% uptime and broad credit triggers) would result in outsized monthly credits for these planned activities.

Request: can Redwood provide a carved-out maintenance window for scheduled batched work (we're proposing up to 4 hours/week if scheduled 72+ hours in advance) and rebalance the monthly credit calculation so that: (a) scheduled maintenance is excluded from downtime calculations when disclosed in advance, and (b) credit calculation prioritizes customer-impacted request counts rather than flat time-based buckets?

We attached our May usage export so you can see the batch profile. Also open to a middle path (lower uptime baseline for batch workloads, e.g., 99.5% rather than 99.9%, with a capped monthly credit).

Can you outline how Redwood would propose to word the carve-out and credit cap (example numbers appreciated)? If helpful, loop in legal/contracting.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudBridge
Attachment: usage_report_may2026.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposal: rebalance of monthly service credit allocation & maintenance carve-out

Hi Samir — thanks for the data and clear ask. I read the export and the nightly spike is apparent. High level options we can offer (open to adjust):

1) Standard hosted SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime, credits triggered by aggregated availability. No carveouts.

2) Batch-friendly SLA: 99.5% monthly uptime baseline for named batch workloads + scheduled maintenance carve-out when windows are announced 72+ hours in advance. Credits calculated only on customer-impacted successful request counts (i.e., exclude periods where no requests would have been processed because of scheduled jobs). Cap: either a fixed percentage of invoice or a monetary cap — example: 15% of monthly service fee OR $30k, whichever is lower.

3) Temporary pilot: 90-day trial where we adopt option (2), monitor customer-impact metrics (p99 latency and error rate), then revert/reevaluate.

I'm attaching a short spreadsheet with credit-cap scenarios (different tiers based on monthly spend) so you can pick a comfortable guardrail. If CloudBridge's legal wants redlines, we'll get contracting involved; looping Marissa (contracts) and Priyom (solutions/ops) to get precise language.

Proposed next step: quick call Thursday to walk example numbers and agree on wording. When would work for you?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sla_credit_options.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: rebalance of monthly service credit allocation & maintenance carve-out

Thanks Samir and Olga — quick note from contracting side. Two drafting thoughts we should consider before legal redlines:

- Credit calculation: instead of completely excluding scheduled maintenance from the uptime denominator, define a clear "scheduled maintenance window" concept (start/end times published 72 hours prior) and count downtime only against the subset of requests that would have been routed to Redwood at that time. Practically, that means credits are proportional to lost successful request volume — avoids large credit transfers for idle windows.

- Cap mechanics: avoid a hard fixed dollar cap that could be gamed; prefer a percent-of-invoice cap with a floor and ceiling (example: min $5k, max 15% of monthly invoice). Also include a clause that credits cannot exceed charges for that service in the month (simple guardrail).

If CloudBridge's legal wants to propose alternate wording, we can iterate. For the Thursday call Olga suggested, I can share a one-pager with a sample credit calculation table.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

From: CloudBridge Legal <legal@cloudbridge.com>

Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Proposal: rebalance of monthly service credit allocation & maintenance carve-out

Olga / Marissa — thanks for the proposal. A few points from our counsel: 

1) Definition: we need precise contract language defining "scheduled maintenance" including who may schedule it (customer vs Redwood), the minimum notice period, and the format (calendar invite + RFC).

2) Cap: CloudBridge prefers a cap equal to 20% of the monthly Redwood bill with a carry-forward option (unused credits can be applied to the next two billing cycles). Our concern is long tails from repeated outages — the carry-forward protects both parties.

3) Metrics: downtime tied to both availability (percent of operational minutes) and observable customer-impact (failed request counts). We propose p99 latency thresholds as an additional trigger for partial credits.

I've attached our redline suggestions (page 2 has the maintenance definition we prefer). If you can provide counterlanguage, we'll get our outside counsel in the loop.

Regards,
CloudBridge Legal
Attachment: cloudbridge_sla_redlines.pdf (PDF, 55KB)
